question.text: Before listing a close-ended Cat III AIF scheme on a stock exchange, which approval sequence is correct?

answer.text: SEBI approval first, then stock exchange in-principle, then final listing
Stock exchange in-principle approval, then SEBI approval, then stock exchange final approval and listing
Only stock exchange approval is needed

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 5.10: Step 1 is application to stock exchange; Step 2 is in-principle approval; Step 3 is SEBI approval; Step 4 is final listing approval by the exchange. The Trap: SEBI approval is obtained AFTER exchange in-principle. Merchant banker certification is unrelated to listing. Cross-Exam Context: Closely parallels listing of REIT/InvIT units (XIX-A scope also).
